topic: Binary Counting and the Towers of Hanoi: The Hidden Logic of Recursion
target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and discrete mathematics

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Bits
lecture_lines: Binary numbers rely on powers of two.
Each bit represents a simple decision.
Three bits count from zero to seven.
animations: Display three empty squares in a row labeled Bit 1, Bit 2, Bit 3 in #FFFFFF using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg].
Highlight Bit 1 square in #FFFF00 for binary 001.
Highlight Bit 2 square in #FFFF00 for binary 010.

sections.title: The Towers of Hanoi Challenge
lecture_lines: Never place large disks on small ones.
The minimum moves follow two to the n minus one.
A three-disk stack takes seven moves.
The puzzle reveals a recursive pattern.
animations: Display three [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/peg.svg] pegs (A, B, C) with a 3-[Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] stack on Peg A in #0000FF.
Highlight 'No large disk on small disk' constraint with a red #FF0000 flash.
Display MathTex 'Moves = 2^n - 1' at the top in #FFFFFF.
Animate a 3-[Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] movement sequence to Peg C.
Show final state with all 3 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] disks on Peg C.

sections.title: Mapping Moves to Binary
lecture_lines: Each binary count step mirrors one move.
The changing bit dictates the disk moved.
The counter maps perfectly to the puzzle.
We watch the binary counter tick up.
Physical movement aligns with abstract counting.
animations: Animate binary counter step 1 (000 to 001) with a movement of the smallest [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg].
Animate binary counter step 2 (001 to 010) with a movement of the second [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg].
Animate binary counter step 3 (010 to 011) with a movement of the smallest [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg].

Animate binary counter step 4 (011 to 100) with a movement of the third (largest) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] on the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg].

sections.title: Algorithmic Symmetry
lecture_lines: Exactly one bit changes each time.
Only one disk moves per step.
The largest disk moves at four.
animations: Display a sequential chain of binary codes from 001 to 111.
Highlight the exact bit that changes between each consecutive step in #00FF00.
Draw an arrow mapping each bit position to its corresponding disk size using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg].

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: The puzzle is a physical binary counter.
Three disks require two cubed minus one moves.
Recursive problem solving is binary logic.
animations: Connect \"Binary Counting\" and \"Recursive Movement\" with a dashed line.
Flash both concepts in #FFFF00 to signify equivalence, revealing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/puzzle.svg].
